edges.subject: danon
edges.evidence: Danon disease is caused by variants (also called mutations) in the LAMP2 gene.

corroboratedBy.evidence: we conclude that primary LAMP-2 deficiency is the cause of Danon disease

edges.subject: LAMP2
edges.evidence: primary deficiencies of LAMP-2, a principal lysosomal membrane protein

corroboratedBy.evidence: this protein is found in the membrane of cellular structures called lysosomes

edges.subject: LAMP2
edges.evidence: The LAMP-2 protein helps transport cellular materials or digestive enzymes into the lysosome

edges.subject: LAMP2
edges.evidence: in cells without the LAMP-2 protein, fusion between autophagic vacuoles and lysosomes occurs more slowly, which leads to the accumulation of autophagic vacuoles

corroboratedBy.evidence: These findings indicate that LAMP-2 is critical for autophagy.

edges.subject: danon
edges.evidence: People with Danon disease have an abnormally large number of autophagic vacuoles in their heart and skeletal muscle cells.

corroboratedBy.evidence: The pathological hallmark of the disease is intracytoplasmic vacuoles containing autophagic material and glycogen in skeletal and cardiac muscle cells.

edges.subject: danon
edges.evidence: The pathological hallmark of the disease is intracytoplasmic vacuoles containing autophagic material and glycogen in skeletal and cardiac muscle cells.

corroboratedBy.evidence: LAMP2 mutations typically cause multisystem glycogen-storage disease (Danon's disease)

edges.subject: pompe
edges.evidence: Mutations in the GAA gene cause Pompe disease.

corroboratedBy.source: Lim, Li & Raben, Front Aging Neurosci 2014 (PMID 25183957)
corroboratedBy.evidence: Pompe disease is a lysosomal storage disorder in which acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) is deficient or absent.

edges.subject: GAA
edges.evidence: Pompe disease is a progressive metabolic neuromuscular disorder resulting from deficiency of lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA).

corroboratedBy.source: Lim, Li & Raben, Front Aging Neurosci 2014 (PMID 25183957)
corroboratedBy.evidence: Deficiency of this lysosomal enzyme results in progressive expansion of glycogen-filled lysosomes in multiple tissues

edges.subject: GAA
edges.source: Lim, Li & Raben, Front Aging Neurosci 2014 (PMID 25183957)
edges.evidence: Deficiency of this lysosomal enzyme results in progressive expansion of glycogen-filled lysosomes in multiple tissues

edges.subject: pompe
edges.source: Lim, Li & Raben, Front Aging Neurosci 2014 (PMID 25183957)
edges.evidence: progressive expansion of glycogen-filled lysosomes in multiple tissues, with cardiac and skeletal muscle being the most severely affected

corroboratedBy.evidence: Mutations in the GAA gene prevent acid alpha-glucosidase from breaking down glycogen effectively, which allows this sugar to build up to toxic levels in lysosomes.

edges.subject: GAA
edges.source: Lim, Li & Raben, Front Aging Neurosci 2014 (PMID 25183957)
edges.evidence: The autophagic process in Pompe skeletal muscle is affected at the termination stage-impaired autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion.

edges.subject: pompe
edges.source: Lim, Li & Raben, Front Aging Neurosci 2014 (PMID 25183957)
edges.evidence: The massive autophagic buildup and lipofuscin inclusions appear to cause a greater effect on muscle architecture than the enlarged lysosomes outside the autophagic regions.

edges.subject: prkag2
edges.source: Arad et al., J Clin Invest 2002 (PMID 11827995)
edges.evidence: Mutations in PRKAG2, the gene for the gamma 2 regulatory subunit of AMP-activated protein kinase, cause cardiac hypertrophy and electrophysiologic abnormalities

corroboratedBy.evidence: Some people with these mutations also have features of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

edges.subject: PRKAG2
edges.evidence: The PRKAG2 gene provides instructions for making one part (the gamma-2 subunit) of a larger enzyme called AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK).

edges.subject: PRKAG2
edges.evidence: AMP-activated protein kinase regulates chemical pathways involving the cell's main energy source, a molecule called adenosine triphosphate (ATP).

edges.subject: prkag2
edges.evidence: changes in AMP-activated protein kinase activity allow a complex sugar called glycogen to build up abnormally within cardiac muscle cells

corroboratedBy.source: Arad et al., J Clin Invest 2002 (PMID 11827995)
corroboratedBy.evidence: Several lines of evidence indicated these vacuoles were filled with glycogen-associated granules.

edges.subject: prkag2
edges.label: a metabolic storage disease driven by constitutively active AMP kinase, not a sarcomere disease
edges.source: Arad et al., J Clin Invest 2002 (PMID 11827995)
edges.evidence: our data indicate that PRKAG2 mutations do not cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy but rather lead to a novel myocardial metabolic storage disease

edges.subject: danon
edges.evidence: The glycogen-storage cardiomyopathy produced by LAMP2 or PRKAG2 mutations resembles hypertrophic cardiomyopathy but is distinguished by electrophysiological abnormalities, particularly ventricular preexcitation.

edges.subject: danon
edges.evidence: LAMP2 mutations typically cause multisystem glycogen-storage disease (Danon's disease) but can also present as a primary cardiomyopathy.

edges.subject: danon
edges.label: Danon is caused by loss of a structural lysosomal protein; Pompe by loss of a lysosomal enzyme
edges.evidence: To our knowledge this is the first example of human cardiopathy-myopathy that is caused by mutations in a lysosomal structural protein rather than an enzymatic protein.

edges.subject: danon
edges.label: normal acid maltase, the enzyme that is deficient in Pompe disease
edges.evidence: "Lysosomal glycogen storage disease with normal acid maltase" which was originally described by Danon et al., is characterized clinically by cardiomyopathy, myopathy and variable mental retardation.

corroboratedBy.evidence: The GAA gene provides instructions for producing an enzyme called acid alpha-glucosidase (also known as acid maltase).

edges.subject: prkag2
edges.label: PRKAG2 histology lacks the myocyte disarray of sarcomeric HCM
edges.source: Arad et al., J Clin Invest 2002 (PMID 11827995)
edges.evidence: these mutations were not associated with myocyte and myofibrillar disarray, the pathognomonic features of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy caused by sarcomere protein mutations
